t: Find the Middle Index in Array - One-Pass Prefix Sum
o: We need the smallest index whose left-side sum equals its right-side sum, with empty sides counting as 0. In Example 1, [2,3,-1,8,4] at index 3 has left sum 2+3-1 = 4 and right sum 4, so the answer is 3. In Example 2, [1,-1,4] at the last index has both sides 0. Example 3 ([2,5]) never balances and returns -1. This is exactly the classic pivot-index pattern: since n is only up to 100, even rescanning both sides per index works, but the standard identity right(i) = total - left(i-1) - nums[i] yields a single extra pass with constant memory.
k: middleIndex is the classic pivot index: balance at i means 2 * left == total - nums[i].
Compute the total once, then sweep once while maintaining a running left sum.
Returning the first hit automatically satisfies the leftmost requirement.
w: Go straight to the running prefix sum; mention brute force only as the naive baseline. Pitfalls: forgetting to exclude the current element from BOTH sides (use total - left - nums[i], not total - left), scanning for the rightmost instead of the leftmost hit, and misreading the edge semantics - index 0 and the last index legitimately have an empty side equal to 0, so any single-element array answers 0. Values are small enough that overflow is not a concern here. Follow-ups: pivot by equal products, multiple balance points (count them all), or the circular-array variant.

a.n: Approach 1: Rescan Both Sides for Each Index
a.i: For every candidate index, directly compute the sum of elements before it and after it and compare. This mirrors the definition word for word, needs no insight, and is perfectly adequate for n <= 100, but it repeats work quadratically.
s: Iterate candidate indices from left to right.
Sum elements strictly before the index and strictly after it.
Return the first index where the two sums match.
a.t: O(n^2) - each of the n candidates rescans up to 2n elements

a.n: Approach 2: Total Plus Running Left Sum
a.i: Let total be the array sum and maintain left, the sum of elements before the current index. The right side is then total - left - nums[i] without any second pass, so one sweep checks every index in O(1). Scanning from the left and returning immediately guarantees the leftmost answer.
s: Compute total as the sum of all elements.
Sweep indices with left starting at 0.
At index i, compare left with total - left - nums[i]; return i on equality.
Otherwise add nums[i] to left and continue.
a.t: O(n) - one pass to compute the total plus one sweeping pass
